classification.difficultyReason: The first four parts explicitly scaffold the displacement components; the remaining demand is to recognise their right triangle, find its hypotenuse and convert an inverse-tangent angle to a southeast bearing.

content.prompt: A hiker starts at point $O$ and travels for $6\text{ km}$ on a bearing of $070^\circ\text{T}$ to a point $A$. The hiker wishes to travel from $A$ to a point $B$, which is $15\text{ km}$ due east of $O$. Give answers correct to the nearest hundredth of a kilometre and to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
The eastward component is opposite the $70^\circ$ angle measured from north.

$$\begin{align*}d_E&=6\sin70^\circ\\d_E&\approx5.64\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

The northward component is adjacent to the $70^\circ$ angle.

$$\begin{align*}d_N&=6\cos70^\circ\\d_N&\approx2.05\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

$B$ is $15\text{ km}$ east of $O$. Retain the unrounded component from part a.

$$\begin{align*}e&=15-6\sin70^\circ\\e&\approx9.36\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

$B$ is due east of $O$, so the distance south from $A$ to $B$ equals the distance north from $O$ to $A$.

$$\begin{align*}s&=6\cos70^\circ\\s&\approx2.05\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$9.58\text{ km}$

Use the perpendicular displacement components to find the angle south of east, then use cosine to find $AB$.
answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle that $AB$ makes south of east. Use the unrounded eastward and southward components.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{6\cos70^\circ}{15-6\sin70^\circ}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{6\cos70^\circ}{15-6\sin70^\circ}\right)\end{align*}$$

The eastward component is adjacent to $\theta$, and $AB$ is the hypotenuse.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{15-6\sin70^\circ}{AB}\\AB\cos\theta&=15-6\sin70^\circ\\AB&=\frac{15-6\sin70^\circ}{\cos\theta}\\AB&\approx9.58\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: On what bearing does the hiker travel if she walks directly from $A$ to $B$?

answer.short:
$102^\circ\text{T}$

Find the angle south of east and add it to $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
From $A$, $B$ lies east and south. Let $\theta$ be the angle south of east.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{6\cos70^\circ}{15-6\sin70^\circ}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{6\cos70^\circ}{15-6\sin70^\circ}\right)\end{align*}$$

True bearings are measured clockwise from north.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=90^\circ+\theta\\\text{Bearing}&\approx102^\circ\text{T}\end{align*}$$
